acceptanceCriteria: benchmarks/runner emits auto-decoy and out-of-scope-probe rows for the development corpus with the metrics above, and benchmarks/README.md documents them as development diagnostics.
The decoys and probes are committed as development cases with their review marks; the current engine's rates are recorded in a build-log entry as the baseline.
A focused test proves a case whose decoy is admitted is reported as a violation and a probe answered READY is reported as a false READY.
body: Decision 0427 / build-log 2026-10-01. The 24-case development corpus carries no must-exclude selector, so the sibling class of blind-v6's forbidden hits was invisible during development, and the 45 cross-repository transplant probes measure the wrong thing (declarations carrying two task words in their own names). Add to benchmarks/runner a generated, labelled auto-decoy set per positive case (the same-file declaration sharing the most name parts with each target, the adjacent declaration, and the same-named symbol elsewhere), reviewed once by a human who may strike a decoy that is genuinely relevant, plus about 12 within-repository out-of-scope probes per development repository (a feature the repository lacks beside ones it has, for example cobra `render command docs as JSON files`, which the current floor answers READY with command.go:Command). Report must-exclude violations over all emitted results and over top-5 separately, abstention precision and recall separately, and a false-READY rate, as diagnostic rows that never gate a release. Nothing here may read the held-out partitions.
title: Generate development must-exclude decoys and a within-repository out-of-scope probe set for the retrieval runner
